Q1.evidence: Order.java, Coupon.java, Product.java, *Repository.java, OrderController.java all use jakarta.persistence.* / jakarta.servlet.*; no javax.* imports

Q2.evidence: OrderApplication is in com.example.order; all components are in com.example.order.* subpackages (common, coupon, idempotency, order, payment, product)

Q3.evidence: build.gradle: only web/validation/data-jpa starters plus flyway-core/flyway-database-postgresql, postgresql, and testcontainers; nothing added separately that a starter already covers

Q4.evidence: idempotency/IdempotencyService.java execute()/replay()/store(): the service builds and returns ResponseEntity and uses HttpHeaders (depends on the web layer)

Q5.evidence: All controllers/services/components (OrderService, OrderController, CouponController, ProductController, IdempotencyService, PaymentGatewayClient, OrderExpiryScheduler) use constructor injection with final fields; no @Autowired

Q6.evidence: Request/response bodies are records such as CouponController.CreateCouponRequest/CouponResponse, ProductController.CreateProductRequest/ProductResponse, OrderController.CreateOrderRequest/PayRequest and OrderResponse; no entities are exposed directly

Q7.evidence: CouponController.create, ProductController.create, OrderController.create/pay: request DTOs have no Bean Validation annotations, @RequestBody has no @Valid, validation is hand-written

Q8.evidence: CouponController.create/get: direct CouponRepository/TransactionTemplate access and validation logic; ProductController.create/get: @Transactional and direct ProductRepository access

Q9.evidence: product/ProductController.java create()/get() have @Transactional on the controller; OrderService.get/list read-only queries do not use readOnly (TransactionTemplate)

Q10.evidence: order/OrderService.pay(): new ApiException(HttpStatus.PAYMENT_REQUIRED, ...); idempotency/IdempotencyService.acquire()/execute(): uses HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY and ResponseEntity

Q11.evidence: common/GlobalExceptionHandler (@RestControllerAdvice) converts ApiException and framework exceptions to HTTP responses in one place

Q12.evidence: common/GlobalExceptionHandler.problem(): builds the response body with a custom record common/Problem, not Spring ProblemDetail

Q13.evidence: GlobalExceptionHandler.handleApi/handleUnreadable and ApiException.validation(): 400 responses carry a single detail string with no per-field error info

Q14.evidence: common/GlobalExceptionHandler.handleUnexpected(): only logs the exception and returns the fixed message "Unexpected server error"

Q15.evidence: Order/Coupon/Product entities have no @ManyToOne/@OneToOne mappings (only @ElementCollection on Order.items)

Q16.evidence: order/OrderService.list(): Order.items has @BatchSize(size=100) and OrderResponse.of is called inside tx.execute, so lazy collections are accessed within the transaction

Q17.evidence: application.yml: datasource url/username/password and payment.gateway.url are injected via ${ENV:default}; PaymentGatewayClient injects them via @Value

Q20.evidence: payment/PaymentGatewayClient constructor @Value(payment.gateway.url/timeout), order/OrderService constructor @Value(order.payment-ttl), OrderExpiryScheduler ${order.expiry-check-interval-ms}: scattered @Value instead of @ConfigurationProperties
